content: {"summary":"To read a 504 on /checkout at the edge, look at the response flag `UT` which means the upstream didn’t finish within the 15 s route timeout, then compare the total duration and the `x‑envoy‑upstream‑service‑time` and hand off to the owning team. On 9 June 2026 orders‑api‑01 returned 504s because its event‑loop was blocked by synchronous crypto work, so requests exceeded the edge’s 15‑second timeout.","likely_cause":"Upstream request timeout caused by event‑loop blockage on orders‑api‑01 due to synchronous crypto work","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"A 504 flag at the edge is `UT`, meaning upstream request timeout when the upstream didn’t finish within the 15 s route timeout.","evidence_ids":["RB-014#0"],"quote":"Upstream request timeout: the upstream didn't finish within the 15 s route timeout"},{"text":"During the 9 June 2026 incident orders‑api‑01 never finished inside the edge’s 15 s limit, resulting in 504 responses.","evidence_ids":["INC-0166#0"],"quote":"orders-api-01 never finished inside that time"},{"text":"The blockage was caused by synchronous crypto work that kept the Node.js event loop busy.","evidence_ids":["INC-0166#0"],"quote":"When a handler does synchronous crypto work, the loop is busy"},{"text":"504 responses began at 13:05 and stopped at 13:30 UTC for orders‑api‑01.","evidence_ids":["INC-0166#2"],"quote":"13:05 | `504` responses begin at the edge for requests that went to orders-api-01"}],"next_checks":["Check edge‑gateway access logs for flag UT and upstream cluster for /checkout","Inspect orders‑api‑01 CPU and event‑loop for long‑running sync crypto calls","Compare total duration vs x‑envoy‑upstream‑service‑time in edge logs","Verify whether other orders‑api pods showed similar 504s"]}
